stories.Headline: I cofounded GPTZero. Now I feel profound sadness about AI and the internet.
stories.Summary:
Edward Tian, the 26-year-old cofounder of GPTZero, has described how his company grew from a tool he built with his cofounder Alex over winter break into a business that was sold to Superhuman. Tian and Alex built the first version of their AI detection tool in January 2023, shortly after ChatGPT was released. The tool became popular almost immediately, and the founders put it on a waitlist, which they say helped build hype. The company later raised about $3.5 million in its first funding round, and it was eventually sold to Superhuman, a pro-AI company. Tian has stayed on at Superhuman as a director of product.

Tian says he never intended to become a founder, since he had planned a journalism career and had a visual investigations fellowship lined up at The New York Times, which he ultimately did not take. He was studying computer science at Princeton and working with a professor at the Princeton Natural Language Processing Lab when the project began. According to the article, the company was not built to remove AI from the internet, and Tian's view of AI has shifted since then. He now says he feels a deep sadness about the state of online writing. He also argues that people should disclose when content is AI-generated, and that authenticity matters more than banning the technology.

Tian points to a growing reliance on AI among people who finished university after ChatGPT launched, particularly in writing. He says that if he were starting college now, he would likely study journalism with a minor in computer science, because humanities skills now matter more. At work, he has noticed colleagues who cannot write or edit well and whose messages read as machine-generated. Part of his current role at Superhuman involves developing responsible AI usage policies and guidance. He emphasizes that people may use these tools as they choose, but he believes it is important to keep human-written content available online.

Articles.Title: I cofounded GPTZero. Now I feel profound sadness about AI and the internet.

stories.Headline: AI Breaks the Traditional Relationship Between Business Growth and Hiring
stories.Summary:
Artificial intelligence is changing how small businesses think about growth, according to a PYMNTS Intelligence analysis published on October 27, 2026. The report, titled "New Data Shows Small Businesses Use AI to Grow Without Hiring" and part of the SMB Growth Monitor, found that 60% of small and medium-sized businesses using AI said they can produce more without adding employees. Among growing businesses, 16% reported skipping a full-time hire because of AI, compared with 10% of businesses with flat revenue. The findings suggest that AI's biggest labor market effect may be the jobs companies no longer need to create rather than the workers they cut.

Traditionally, a small business that expanded its revenue also needed more people to serve customers, process transactions, and deliver services. Now automation can absorb added workloads, such as handling more customer inquiries, producing more marketing material, or reconciling more transactions, without hiring. The disruption also runs in both directions, since a company's efficiency gain can become a rival's lost sale. Frequent AI users in the data estimated savings equal to 16% of annual revenue from avoiding outside help, but they also estimated losing revenue equal to 6.7% as customers turned to AI instead of buying their services.

The article presents this as a reallocation of business spending rather than a simple drop in headcount, and it argues that growth may depend more on where companies deploy human expertise than on how many people they employ. Its authors, the PYMNTS Intelligence researchers behind the SMB Growth Monitor, frame the next competitive edge as making remaining human work more valuable. The report found that 23% of SMBs gained customers specifically seeking human-delivered work, 14% attracted business correcting AI-generated output, and another 21% emphasized human involvement as a selling point or planned to do so. The piece offers an example of an accounting firm that may lose routine bookkeeping but gain demand for complex financial judgment.

Articles.Title: AI Breaks the Traditional Relationship Between Business Growth and Hiring

stories.Headline: Lenders are done financing AI on faith, JPMorgan says
stories.Summary:
Lenders have stopped treating an AI label as enough to secure financing, according to a JPMorgan report published October 23, 2026. Justin Biemann, global investment strategist at J.P. Morgan Private Bank, wrote that companies now have to show they can fund investment, service their debt and eventually turn spending into cash flow. The report was reported by CoinDesk on October 27, 2026. The shift follows record costs for insuring debt at several AI-linked firms.

Credit default swap trading tied to major AI companies rose sharply, with Morgan Stanley data showing weekly volumes averaging more than $9 billion in September, up from under $2 billion a week in July. The report cites one financing-dependent AI infrastructure company whose five-year CDS reached 1,100 basis points, meaning insuring $10 million of its debt would cost more than $1 million a year. Biemann wrote that pricing at that level implies near or above a 50% probability of default over five years, up from below 30% a year earlier. Large AI leaders with strong cash flow pay 50 to 120 basis points for similar protection, while some established infrastructure borrowers have climbed toward 300 basis points.

Biemann said the stress is concentrated in business models that depend on debt markets staying open while spending stays high and cash flow stays limited. He compared today's CDS levels to the run-up before Lehman Brothers' 2008 bankruptcy, describing them as warning lights rather than countdown clocks. He argued that activity in the large AI leaders' CDS looks more like hedging than a prediction of distress. Elon Musk separately warned on a Sunday that debt funding is drying up for AI neoclouds.

CoinDesk linked the concern to crypto because AI has been a major driver of risk-taking across markets, including bitcoin. JPMorgan warned that a deeper AI downturn could spill into other risk assets. The Nasdaq had fallen 6.7% to 29,263 from 31,360 since October 6, with AI-linked firms such as Nvidia and Oracle dropping more than the index. The articles do not say what comes next for the sector.

Articles.Title: Lenders are done financing AI on faith, JPMorgan says

stories.Headline: Chip Stocks Rebound 4-5% as AI Profitability Fears Ease
stories.Summary:
Shares of chipmakers in South Korea rebounded sharply after a period of heavy swings, with the KOSPI closing at 5,638.34 on the 27th, up 168.87 points or 3.09%. Samsung Electronics ended at 222,000 won, up 4.23%, and SK hynix finished at 1.341 million won, up 5.18%. The rally followed favorable news from Anthropic and eased worries that returns on AI investment would fall short. Investors had been unsettled by a dispute over whether spending on AI infrastructure would pay off.

Brokerages argued that the concerns had gone too far. Hwang Seung-taek of Hana Securities said interest costs at large technology firms amount to only 2% to 3% of operating cash flow, leaving them able to keep investing even if rates rise. Analysts also expected operating profit at South Korean chipmakers to rise about 50% next year. Still, a sustained rally would depend on the recovery spreading beyond high-bandwidth memory to conventional memory chips.

Separately, Anthropic said in a registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on the 26th that its investment contracts with chip and data center companies total more than $800 billion, with the investment period extending to 2045. The company reported that first-half revenue rose more than 14-fold from a year earlier to $16.286 billion, and that adjusted operating profit of $1.618 billion marked its first half-year profit since its founding. Wall Street has said the company must prove it can generate profits to cover that spending if it is to complete the largest initial public offering on record. Anthropic also said participation in the offering is restricted in South Korea because it has not completed registration procedures under local law.

Trading data also showed a sharp drop in short positions. The combined stock lending balance for Samsung Electronics and SK hynix fell by 11.0854 trillion won, or 26.1%, to 31.4581 trillion won as of the 26th, and a financial investment industry official said existing short sellers may have moved to buy back shares to close positions. Net short-selling balances fell even more steeply, with SK hynix's dropping 97.4% to 11.0 billion won from 415.6 billion won on the 1st of the month. The articles describe these moves as part of the broader shift in sentiment behind the rebound.

Articles.Title: Chip Stocks Rebound 4-5% as AI Profitability Fears Ease - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: SK Draws 4,000 to AI Training Program Paying 3 Million Won a Month
stories.Summary:
SK Group drew about 4,000 people to an information session on AIGEN, a new two-year non-degree AI education program. The turnout was large enough that organizers moved the event from a venue planned for 130 people to a live YouTube broadcast. The program is open to young adults aged 19 to 34 regardless of educational background or major, and applicants need no coding experience. It pays a 3 million won growth stipend each month for two years and provides customized education and mentoring in cooperation with Seoul National University's AI Institute.

Applications for the first cohort open from the 1st to the 15th of next month, and about 50 people are to be selected by late December. The program is set to begin in March 2027. Unlike programs tied to a job at a specific company or a degree, AIGEN emphasizes building the ability to identify and solve problems using AI. The articles present it as a break from the older practice of companies training employees only after hiring them.

The articles attribute the program to SK Group and do not quote any executive describing its goals in detail. Separately, Lotte Group announced the Lotte AX Challenge 2026, an AI competition linked to hiring that is open regardless of education or age, with OpenAI providing technical support and serving as a judge. Preliminary entries run from the 28th of this month to the 4th of next month, and seven winners will share 20 million won in prizes and receive internships that can convert to full-time jobs. The final round is set for the 24th and 25th of next month at Lotte's Osan campus.

The articles place these moves alongside wage data showing a widening gap. In the first half of 2026, the share of wage workers averaging 5 million won or more a month reached a record 17.6%, while the share earning under 1 million won also rose, to 9.8%. High-pay shares were highest in finance and insurance at 40.5% and in information and communications at 35.8%. The articles also note that Microsoft is running a voluntary retirement program for up to about 60,000 employees while it spends heavily on AI.

Articles.Title: SK Draws 4,000 to AI Training Program Paying 3 Million Won a Month - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: LG Uplus to Set Liquid Cooling Standards for AI Data Centers
stories.Summary:
LG Uplus, the South Korean telecom operator, and Ecolab Korea, a water treatment solutions provider, signed a memorandum of understanding on October 27, 2026, at LG Uplus's Yongsan office in Seoul to develop operating standards for liquid cooling in next-generation AI data centers. The two companies plan to build an integrated framework covering liquid cooling installation, coolant quality management and real-time monitoring. The aim is to secure the stability and reliability that next-generation AI infrastructure requires. The agreement was reported by Seoul Economic Daily and is focused on the technical side of running these facilities. Liquid cooling removes heat more efficiently than the air cooling used in conventional data centers, but it can cause equipment failures if coolant quality slips or facilities are poorly managed.

The partners will carry out technical verification of the TCS loop, which connects AI server racks to a coolant distribution unit so that coolant circulates. LG Uplus will supply the large-scale liquid cooling pilot environment it is building at its Pyeongchon 2 center to test AI infrastructure based on next-generation graphics processing unit architecture. Ecolab Korea will set up a coolant quality management system through its digital water quality monitoring platform. LG Uplus and Ecolab Korea will jointly analyze data on coolant condition and on key cooling facilities to find the best operating criteria and management methods. Their goal is a framework that can cool high-density, high-heat AI servers steadily and flag early warning signs in liquid cooling systems.

Jung Sook-kyung, executive director of LG Uplus's AI data center business, said the partnership would secure liquid cooling operating standards and a quality management system. She added that the work would give customers a more stable and reliable AI data center operating environment. The article places the agreement within a wave of investment in AI data center infrastructure, noting related moves by Elice, NAVER and Schneider Electric. It does not give a timeline for the verification work, the pilot results or when the standards will be published. The article also does not give financial terms of the agreement.

Articles.Title: LG Uplus to Set Liquid Cooling Standards for AI Data Centers - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Unframe Removes Another Barrier Between AI Capabilities and Adoption
stories.Summary:
Unframe, an applied AI lab based in Cupertino, California, announced on October 27, 2026, that its software is now available on the AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace and Microsoft Marketplace. The company said the listings let enterprises buy its product through the cloud accounts they already use. Procurement teams can apply committed cloud spend toward Unframe and follow their existing approval workflows. The announcement was distributed through Business Wire as a paid press release.

The company said private offers are available on all three platforms, which allow it to set pricing, contract terms and usage parameters delivered through a customer's cloud account. Unframe described the move as a way to avoid separate vendor contracts, legal reviews and procurement cycles. It also said customers can draw down existing cloud and AI commitments rather than allocating new budget. The company stressed that it does not replace the foundational platforms enterprises already use, including AWS, Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud. It described its product as an application, orchestration and governance layer that sits on top of those platforms.

Jacquelyn Goldberg, Global VP of Revenue at Unframe, was quoted saying that enterprises should not have to choose between moving quickly on AI and working within their current procurement and cloud frameworks. She said the company's job is to close the gap between what AI can do and what enterprises run in production. The company said it delivers tailored, production-ready AI solutions in days with measurable business impact in weeks. Interested enterprises were directed to contact@unframe.ai or to schedule a call, and the media contact listed was Dan Klempay.

The release notes that cloud marketplaces have become a preferred channel for buying software, and that being listed on all three major marketplaces is now a key expectation for enterprise software vendors. Unframe said it is headquartered in Cupertino with a global presence in Tel Aviv and Berlin. The articles do not report any independent assessment of the company's claims or any pricing figures. The release is the company's own promotional material, so no regulatory or third-party response is included.

Articles.Title: Unframe Removes Another Barrier Between AI Capabilities and Adoption

stories.Headline: Oracle Unveils Fusion Agentic Applications for HR, Powered by Fusion Claw
stories.Summary:
Oracle announced on October 27, 2026, at the HR Technology Conference in Las Vegas, a new set of agentic applications for human resources built on a platform it calls Fusion Claw. The Japanese release is an abridged translation of a statement Oracle issued in the United States on October 21. Oracle describes Fusion Claw as an execution foundation with governance built in, which lets the new Fusion Agentic Applications carry out specialized work such as deep research, calculation, simulation, modeling and continuous replanning. The applications sit inside Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications and run on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, using large language models. A second release, published the same day and tied to the Oracle AI World event, says the same technology is being extended across finance, supply chain, sales and service as well.

The HR lineup in Oracle Fusion Cloud Human Capital Management covers three areas. For workforce planning and operations, Workforce Orchestration builds staffing plans that weigh changing demand, cost and continuity, while Position Command Center links position, hiring, cost and approval data to flag inconsistencies before they disrupt work. For talent acquisition, Candidate Sourcing sorts candidates and coordinates outreach and follow-up, and Recruiting Command Center pulls together requisition, interview, feedback and offer data to show recruiters what to do next. For compensation and payroll, Workforce Compensation drafts budget-aligned pay plans, Payroll Command Center scans employee data, time cards, retroactive changes and past trends to find likely problems, and Payroll Activity Workspace compares current pay, balances and costs with earlier periods. In each case the application prepares recommended actions for a person to review and approve.

Lewis Thompson, Oracle's senior vice president of applications development, said business and HR leaders struggle to connect and assess all the information on their own as conditions change quickly. He said the new applications reason across Oracle Fusion Applications data, supply relevant context, coordinate the work needed to reach business goals, and carry out actions that people have approved. In a separate statement, Chris Leone, Oracle's executive vice president of applications development, said people should set goals and policies while software takes on more of the work. The second release also says 25 Claw-powered agentic applications are now available across the ERP, HCM, supply chain and customer experience products, and names new AI experiences called Oracle Fusion Companion and Oracle Fusion Agentic Home.

The applications belong to a wider Fusion AI ecosystem centered on Oracle AI Agent Studio for Fusion Applications. Its Fusion Agentic Applications Builder and AI Studio Skill offer no-code and pro-code tools, so organizations can build and manage agentic applications by reusing agents from Oracle, its partners and other outside sources. Built-in observability, return-on-investment measurement and safety controls are meant to keep the agents delivering measurable value under proper oversight. For hiring workflows, Oracle states that organizations remain responsible for employment decisions and can set human oversight, approval steps and controls in line with their own policies and applicable legal requirements. The articles give no pricing and no rollout schedule beyond the availability statement for the 25 applications.

Articles.Title: Oracle pushes outcome-driven AI across Fusion Applications

stories.Headline: TDSE、Databricks 「Data + AI World Tour Tokyo 2026」 ・
stories.Summary:
TDSE株式会社 announced on October 27, 2026 that it will sponsor and exhibit at "Data + AI World Tour Tokyo 2026," an event organized by Databricks Japan, held on Friday, November 27, 2026 at The Prince Park Tower Tokyo. The company is serving as an Explorer sponsor and will run a booth (E-6) and give a lightning talk from 12:15 to 12:30 on a manufacturing analytics agent built on Databricks. The talk, titled "ALL on Databricks," describes how unstructured data such as handwritten forms, inspection records and product catalogs can be used for quality trouble response. The booth will also show a demo of the same agent. The event runs from 9:30 to 19:30, with the Expo open from 9:30 to 17:15, and admission is free with advance registration.

The talk and demo combine three functions, according to the release: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to search past defect cases by meaning, Agent Bricks to organize possible causes and rank them by priority, and a Genie agent that turns natural language into SQL to analyze the affected scope, including shipping destinations and quantities. The demo walks through a single flow of referencing past defects, prioritizing causes and cross-analyzing related lots. Structured and unstructured data are managed under the same governance through Unity Catalog. The company says the approach is part of the data and generative AI expansion goals in its new medium-term plan, "SHIFT2028."

TDSE, a Tokyo company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth market, said it treats Databricks as a priority area and supports customers from building a lakehouse through AI deployment in operations and in-house capability building. The company has 193 employees as of October 1, 2026, and describes its business as integrated AI-centered solutions for companies pursuing data-driven management. Booth visitors can also ask about Databricks adoption, environment setup, AI agent deployment, platform migration and talent development. Event details and registration are available on the official event website.

Articles.Title: TDSE、Databricks 主催「Data + AI World Tour Tokyo 2026」に協賛・出展

stories.Headline: Oracle launches setup and configuration features for Fusion Applications that support AI agents, helping speed up adoption
stories.Summary:
Oracle has released a public Git repository called the Oracle Fusion Setup and Configuration Registry, or FSCR, which lets AI agents read and carry out setup and configuration tasks for Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications. The company announced it on October 26, 2026 at Oracle AI World in Las Vegas, and a Japanese version of the release was published on October 27. The registry packages Oracle's product expertise and best practices as reusable AI skills covering configuration options, dependencies, execution order, and testing and validation. Oracle says this is meant to speed up adoption by automating much of the manual setup work that usually takes a long time during implementation.

According to the release, FSCR is built and maintained by Oracle alongside the Fusion Applications, so customers, partners, and AI agents all draw on the same current source. Agents using it can turn business requirements, process documents, policies, and existing configurations into implementation steps, then carry out the setup or updates directly inside Fusion Applications. They can also test and validate the results automatically, while expert reviewers check the finished configuration, request changes, and approve deployment. System integrators can extend the open foundation with their own methods, accelerators, automation, and industry solutions. The release does not give figures for time saved or the number of skills included.

Chris Leone, Oracle's executive vice president for application development, is quoted as saying that customers and partners often must rebuild setup knowledge for each deployment or rely on documentation that goes stale as new features arrive. He described the registry as a way for product-savvy guidance to walk teams through the entire setup process, with implementation knowledge evolving alongside the product. The release places this within Oracle's broader Fusion Agentic Applications offering, which lets agents run end-to-end business processes within policies and permissions defined by each organization. It also points to Oracle AI Agent Studio for Fusion Applications as the tool customers and partners use to build, extend, and manage such agents. The release does not say when additional skills or updates will be added beyond the ongoing maintenance it describes.

Articles.Title: Oracle launches setup and configuration features for Fusion Applications that support AI agents, helping speed up adoption

stories.Headline: ETRI Develops Korean-Teaching AI That Outperforms GPT Models
stories.Summary:
The Electronics and Telecommunications Research Institute (ETRI) announced on October 28, 2026 that researchers in its Language Intelligence Research Section had built an artificial intelligence system for teaching Korean to foreign learners. The system holds free-flowing conversations with learners while still covering the material scheduled for each lesson. Foreign-language classes follow daily learning goals, but conversations with generative AI tend to drift away from the curriculum, leaving learners to decide what to say next. The institute sought a way to open up free conversation for intermediate and advanced learners without losing track of the curriculum.

The core of the technology is what the researchers call "topic-guided free conversation." Learners are given only the topic, while the AI alone knows the learning steps to be covered within it. The researchers built three mechanisms into the system. One tracks which stage the conversation has reached and decides when to move on, and another filters out questions already asked. A third divides the work so that familiar expressions go to a small ETRI model with between 3 billion and 13 billion parameters, while expressions it has not learned are passed to a general-purpose AI such as GPT.

In a blind evaluation of speaking ability involving 102 people, including foreign learners, Korean-language teachers and experts in AI and language education, ETRI's technology scored highest on the share of learner utterances answered appropriately, at 93.8%. That compared with 91.0% for GPT-4o-mini and 90.9% for GPT-5.1. ETRI's system also had the lowest error rate during conversation, at 18.6%, against 25.4% and 23.7% for the two GPT models, and learners preferred it in eight of 10 scenarios. The GPT models did better at avoiding repeated questions and at varying their expressions.

ETRI is also developing a smart glasses platform that runs its small language model alongside GPT, with the two taking turns responding to users' spoken questions. The researchers plan to improve performance by accumulating user data and optimizing how roles are divided between the two models. They also aim to expand the speaking-focused tutor into a broader "AI Korean teacher" covering reading and writing, tailored to each learner's proficiency and study history. Principal researcher Hwang Geum-ha said many foreigners never reach fluency because they struggle to make Korean friends, and that an AI teacher could play the role of a native-speaker friend. Lim Soo-jong, head of the section, said the institute will develop the system into AI education technology that learners around the world can rely on.

Articles.Title: ETRI Develops Korean-Teaching AI That Outperforms GPT Models - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Opinion: Is AI changing local democracy? We should probably talk about it.
stories.Summary:
This is an opinion column, not a news report, so there is no breaking event to recount. Brandon University assistant professor Jennifer Mateer, writing in the Brandon Sun on October 26, 2026, argues that the municipal election, which was one day away, has a different feel because some campaign signs, social media posts and replies to voters appear to have been made at least partly with generative artificial intelligence. She says she has noticed posters with the glossy finish that image generators tend to produce, and she asks how the community feels about that. Her column is framed as a question for residents to consider rather than a report of any rule or decision.

Mateer acknowledges a fair case for AI use in local politics, since running for city council or school board trustee costs money and many candidates cannot hire a graphic designer or communications consultant. She draws a line between using AI to present ideas, which she sees as less troubling, and using it to develop ideas, such as answering a constituent's question or stating a position on a local issue. She also warns that AI is not neutral, because models trained on materials reflecting existing political and social biases can reproduce those biases, raising the question of whose values voters are actually hearing. She notes that political communications have long relied on speechwriters, but that few municipal candidates have ever had one, so voters could reasonably assume the person at the door and the person answering their email were the same. She points out that cities maintain about 60 per cent of Canada's essential infrastructure, citing the Federation of Canadian Municipalities, and that councils shape decisions like school walking routes and what gets built on vacant lots.

Mateer does not call for a ban on candidates using AI, and she says the apparently AI-generated signs along 18th Street or Victoria Avenue are not necessarily a democratic crisis. Instead, she argues that voters should expect a little transparency, and she asks whether candidates should disclose when they use AI for campaign materials or for responses to voters. She concludes that when residents write to a candidate, they should be able to trust that the reply reflects that candidate's own thinking. The column does not describe any policy change, regulation or response from candidates or city officials, and the article itself does not say what, if anything, will follow the election.

Articles.Title: Opinion: Is AI changing local democracy? We should probably talk about it. - Brandon Sun

stories.Headline: SAP Empowers AI Developers to Build What Matters and Turn Intent into Autonomous Execution
stories.Summary:
SAP SE announced a series of AI innovations on October 27, 2026, at its annual SAP TechEd conference in Berlin, expanding its portfolio for developers. The enhancements cover Joule Studio, Joule Work and the SAP Business AI Platform, including a new tabular foundation model called SAP-RPT-2.0. Together they offer tools to build and extend AI agents, richer business data for those agents to reason with, and stronger governance controls for running them across the enterprise. SAP Business AI Platform gives organizations one place to build, contextualize and govern AI across SAP and third-party environments. Joule Studio lets business users and developers use no-code and pro-code tools to build agents, choosing from more than 70 AI models.

SAP said that customers' data remains their own and that the company does not share customer data with anyone to train or improve large language models. Joule Work gains new agentic thinking capabilities that plan and carry out multistep business workflows across SAP systems. Third-party agents can securely invoke Joule Agents through a governed agent gateway, and a new SAP Enterprise AI Gateway will centralize authentication, policy enforcement, routing, monitoring and auditing of AI traffic. A new AI Governance Assistant is meant to help customers meet compliance requirements under the EU AI Act. Joule Studio will also offer observability and administrative controls covering agent behavior, model usage and spend.

Philipp Herzig, CTO of SAP SE, said the company is moving from AI learning a business to running it, and described Joule Work as the place where users state their intent and get work done. He said the platform is built on more than 50 years of process and industry expertise. SAP also described a partnership with HPE to deploy SAP-RPT on the HPE Spaceborne Computer-2 aboard the International Space Station, where the model is planned to support anomaly triage, predict failures and reconstruct missing sensor values without sending data back to Earth. Other announcements included expanded data partnerships with Dremio and Databricks, and a collaboration with Intel linking enterprise workflows to autonomous robots. Joule Studio's runtime will remain free for select customers through December 2026, according to the release.

Articles.Title: SAP Empowers AI Developers to Build What Matters and Turn Intent into Autonomous Execution - TradingView

stories.Headline: South Korea investors drive Hanwha HBM ETF to top net buys on AI memory boom
stories.Summary:
Hanwha Asset Management said on October 28, 2026 that its PLUS Global HBM Semiconductor exchange-traded fund ranked first among overseas semiconductor ETFs listed in South Korea by net purchases from individual investors this year. As of October 26, individuals had put a net 593.3 billion won into the product since the start of the year. The fund has returned 88.30% so far in 2026, ranking tenth among all domestically listed ETFs, including leveraged and inverse products. Its returns over the past one, two and three years were 135.01%, 368.22% and 526.75%, respectively.

The company said the fund's strategy differs from rival semiconductor ETFs, which are concentrated in two domestic companies. Its core holdings are the three global memory leaders, SK hynix, Samsung Electronics and Micron, with leading global firms weighted evenly to spread risk. In May, a regular rebalancing added SanDisk, a leading NAND company, along with memory-testing and back-end equipment specialists Techwing and Teradyne. The portfolio now spans high bandwidth memory, DRAM, NAND and major equipment makers. Hanwha Asset Management attributed the investor interest partly to the downside protection the fund has offered during market volatility.

Hanwha Asset Management also expects chip demand to keep rising as the AI industry grows. It pointed to a securities registration statement that Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI model, recently filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for an initial public offering, in which Anthropic named semiconductor supply shortages as a key business risk. The company's ETF business head, Geum Jeong-seop, said the top ranking shows investors see memory chips as a structural beneficiary of AI infrastructure growth rather than a short-term theme. He said the company views AI-driven memory growth as having entered a full-fledged phase and pledged stable management and active investor communication. The article was written by Park Ji-youn of Chosunbiz.

Articles.Title: South Korea investors drive Hanwha HBM ETF to top net buys on AI memory boom - Chosunbiz

stories.Headline: SK Hynix Operating Margin Nears 80% on Soaring HBM, Commodity Memory Prices
stories.Summary:
SK Hynix reported third-quarter results that put its operating margin at about 79.7%, a level close to 80%, as demand for artificial intelligence chips and memory prices climbed. Bloomberg reported on October 27 that the company posted operating profit of 83.3333 trillion won ($60.4 billion), up 632.1% from a year earlier. Revenue rose 327.9% to 104.6155 trillion won ($75.8 billion) over the same period. The gains came from higher prices for high-bandwidth memory, known as HBM, and for commodity memory. SK Hynix has benefited from supplying HBM to Nvidia as customers invest more in AI data centers.

Prices for commodity DRAM and NAND flash rose sharply, which boosted profitability alongside HBM. Memory makers have shifted more production toward HBM, which has reduced the supply of commodity memory and helped push prices higher. SK Hynix said the memory shortage will continue through 2030. The company is expanding long-term supply agreements with major customers, including Nvidia. It also announced an additional shareholder return plan worth 100 trillion won ($72.5 billion) for fiscal 2026.

MS Hwang, a director at Counterpoint Research, said HBM prices are rising too, but the sharp jump in earnings came mainly from steep increases in commodity DRAM and NAND prices. Hwang said quarterly earnings have not yet peaked and that the uptrend will likely continue at least through 2027. Macquarie estimates that memory now accounts for about one-third of the cost of building AI data centers. It projects HBM prices will more than double by 2027, which would raise that share further. Demand from expanding AI infrastructure spending is also seen as a positive factor for the sector.

Articles.Title: SK Hynix Operating Margin Nears 80% on Soaring HBM, Commodity Memory Prices - bloomingbit

stories.Headline: HBM explained: the AI memory behind SK Hynix’s record profits and rising chip prices
stories.Summary:
High-bandwidth memory, or HBM, is a type of DRAM that stacks thin memory dies vertically and places them right beside a processor, delivering far more bandwidth with less power. SK Hynix reported third-quarter operating profit of around 83 trillion won, roughly seven times the level of a year earlier, on an operating margin of around 80%. The explainer ties that surge to HBM, which the company's results highlight as a key driver. The article presents the product as the reason behind much of the recent strength in memory prices and earnings. AI chips are often held back less by calculation speed than by how quickly they can receive data.

Every leading AI accelerator, including Nvidia's GPUs, is packaged with HBM for that reason. Making HBM uses far more wafer capacity per unit of memory than standard DRAM, with industry estimates commonly putting it at around three times as much. As production shifts toward HBM, less capacity is left for the conventional DRAM used in PCs, phones and servers, which helps explain the price rises. The article notes that SK Hynix reported DRAM selling prices up by a high-20% rate in a single quarter.

Only SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics and Micron make HBM at scale, and SK Hynix holds the largest share. Citing Counterpoint Research, the article says SK Hynix's share of HBM revenue fell to around 50% in the second quarter of 2026 from around 64% a year earlier, while Samsung's rose to around 33% and Micron held around 18%. The next contest is HBM4, which is being built into Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang said in June that all three suppliers are in production, with the first systems due to ship in the third quarter.

Analysts estimate SK Hynix supplies most of that volume, though Nvidia has not disclosed a split. The article describes HBM as central to record memory profits but also as a cyclical business that could soften as competition and new capacity catch up with demand. Some forecasters warn that prices could ease once supply grows. Investors are told to watch HBM4 volumes and pricing, how quickly Samsung and Micron gain ground, and whether AI spending keeps growing fast enough to absorb new supply.

Articles.Title: HBM explained: the AI memory behind SK Hynix’s record profits and rising chip prices - investingLive

stories.Headline: AI Investment in Australia and New Zealand Drives Data Focus
stories.Summary:
Organisations across Australia and New Zealand are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence, but a recent Boomi-Omdia study suggests that spending on AI does not automatically produce measurable business value. Over 70% of Australian organisations and around 65% of New Zealand organisations reported active AI initiatives. Yet close to 30% of respondents in Australia and more than 30% in New Zealand said they could not estimate AI success effectively. The study also found that 39% of Australian and 43% of New Zealand organisations lacked a dedicated AI budget, even though many planned to increase spending soon.

The article argues that the weak point is the data beneath AI systems rather than the tools themselves. Poor ownership, inconsistent records, fragmented information and weak integration can all degrade the output of an AI model. It points to a financial institution whose customer details sit in several systems under slightly different names, which could lead an AI model to treat one customer as several people. The article says that around 90% of organisations across the region are considering heavy investment in AI risk, governance and compliance, but fewer than half have formal AI governance policies. It adds that more than 90% consider data integration a priority, while fewer than half use a platform-driven approach to it.

The writer recommends that businesses check whether the information feeding AI is trustworthy, accessible and consistent before buying more tools. Governance should be built in when a system is selected, deployed and monitored, rather than added after problems appear. The article also says that over 70% of organisations report that unmanaged shadow integrations, built for short-term needs, are harming data quality and trust. It advises categorising data by sensitivity, defining access permissions, and setting baseline metrics such as duplicate rates, error rates and cost per transaction so that real gains can be separated from activity that only looks innovative. It also notes that the New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment treats data quality as a priority for responsible AI use.

Articles.Title: AI Investment in Australia and New Zealand Drives Data Focus - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Why Isn't AI Smarter About Data Centers | Newsradio 600 KOGO | Cliff Notes on the News
stories.Summary:
San Diego Mayor Todd Gloria has signed an executive order placing a moratorium on any new AI data centers in the city, and the council appears to support the move. The action comes as the issue has become a major source of controversy in the city during the final week of October 2026. Data centers, which are specialized facilities built to handle the heavy computing demands of training and running artificial intelligence models, have drawn fierce opposition across the region and the country. Critics point to massive resource demands, environmental impacts, and disruptions to quality of life. The story was reported on October 27, 2026.

In his statement on Monday, Gloria said he believes San Diego can embrace emerging technologies and attract good-paying jobs while still protecting the quality of life that makes the city special. His position reflects a balance between welcoming new technology and guarding local residents against its side effects. Local leaders across the country are facing the same questions about these facilities. The article suggests that regulations and tough guidelines for new data centers are likely to follow in many places. The moratorium in San Diego applies to new projects, leaving the wider rules still to be developed.

The article also raises a lighter point about the irony of the situation. The author notes that AI models should be smart enough to recognize the scrutiny these facilities are facing. That observation is offered as commentary rather than as reported fact. The piece was written by veteran San Diego news director and reporter Cliff Albert as part of his weekday segment on Newsradio 600 KOGO. It draws on the broader debate about how cities should respond to rapid growth in AI infrastructure.

Articles.Title: Why Isn't AI Smarter About Data Centers | Newsradio 600 KOGO | Cliff Notes on the News - Newsradio 600 KOGO

stories.Headline: DOW Releases Unbiased AI Procurement Guidance, Templates
stories.Summary:
The Department of War released template contract language and documentation tools on Tuesday, October 26, 2026, to hold artificial intelligence vendors to federal standards for accuracy and political neutrality. A memo signed by John Tenaglia, principal director of defense pricing, contracting, and acquisition policy, said the guidance carries out Executive Order 14319, Preventing Woke AI in the Federal Government, and Office of Management and Budget Memorandum M-26-04. Compliance with both is required, though components may adapt or skip the templates depending on how complex and risky a purchase is. The guidance has three attachments that together shape how buyers select, document, and enforce AI contracts. Under the first attachment, a requiring activity signs a memo classifying its purchase as a large language model, another generative AI model, discriminative AI, or none of these.

That classification determines which transparency documents vendors must provide. The second attachment turns those choices into Section L proposal instructions, and the third places compliance terms into the statement of work or performance work statement. For large language model purchases, offerors must submit the developer's acceptable use policy, current model, system or data cards, end-user resources, and a channel for the government to give feedback on problematic outputs. Officials handling higher-risk requirements may also request red-teaming results, system prompts, bias benchmarks, foreign training work, and changes made to meet other governments' rules.

The guidance treats compliance as a material requirement, which ties it to vendor eligibility and payment and allows termination for default if a vendor refuses to fix problems. When outputs appear to breach the principles, the contracting officer notifies the contractor, and the contractor then has 15 business days to report its findings, the likely cause, its proposed fixes, and a schedule. Vendors must also update their documentation after significant model changes and pass the terms down to subcontracts at every tier. The memo was signed by Tenaglia, and the articles do not say whether any individual vendor has been notified under these provisions.

The guidance also arrives amid earlier criticism: in April, the Government Accountability Office reported that agencies lacked data scientists to evaluate vendor proposals and struggled to understand AI costs. GAO further found that four agencies, the Department of War, the General Services Administration, and the departments of Homeland Security and Veterans Affairs, could not meet an OMB requirement to share procurement lessons learned because their internal policies barred collecting them. The articles do not describe what steps those agencies plan to take to resolve that conflict. They also do not say when the templates will first be used in an actual solicitation or how many contracts are expected to adopt them.
